items.title: 8.12 The effect of a change of concentration

blocks.text: If a system at equilibrium has some of a reactant or product added or removed, the equilibrium position is disturbed. There are four possibilities. Consider the hydrolysis of bismuth chloride, BiCl3 + H2O giving BiOCl + 2HCl, in which BiCl3 reacts with water to give the white insoluble compound BiOCl; the expression is Kc = [BiOCl][HCl]^2 / ([BiCl3][H2O]) as printed. When water is added to a BiCl3 solution it turns cloudy with the white precipitate; at equilibrium some BiOCl and HCl have formed and some BiCl3 remains.

items: Adding BiCl3 or water disturbs the equilibrium; to re-establish it more BiOCl and HCl are produced, the reaction is pushed forward, Kc stays constant but the position changes.
Adding BiOCl or HCl or both: more BiCl3 is produced and the reaction moves in the reverse direction; Kc constant, position changed.
Removing some BiCl3: the reaction moves in the reverse direction to compensate; a new position with Kc constant.
Removing BiOCl or HCl or both: the reaction moves forward to compensate; a new position, Kc constant.

blocks.prompt: For 2H2(g) + O2(g) giving 2H2O(g) at equilibrium, what happens to the concentrations of H2 and O2 if more water vapour is added?
blocks.explanation: Adding a product disturbs the equilibrium, which shifts to the left to use up some of the added water. H2 and O2 are formed in the process, so their concentrations increase, while Kc is unchanged.

items: Add a reactant or remove a product: shift forward; add a product or remove a reactant: shift backward (BiCl3 hydrolysis, white BiOCl appearing or dissolving); the position changes, Kc does not.
